title: move lets an agent or the store reject or snooze a card; only accept is guarded
body:
## Summary
Guard `verified|pushed -> rejected|snoozed` (and merge into a card the agent did not find as a same-work duplicate) to `human:` and `forge:` deciders in DECIDER_GUARDS, as SKILL.md and triage.md state, so a rejection can never come from the agent.

## Description
SKILL.md:544 says "Only a human accepts, rejects, snoozes or merges into another person's item", and skill/references/triage.md:14-15 list `verified -> rejected` and `verified -> snoozed` as "human". The code guards only acceptance: skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:101-103 `DECIDER_GUARDS = { 'verified>accepted': ['human'] }`, checked at skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:348. `triage apply` requires `human:` (skill/scripts/lib/triage.mjs:133) and so do rules (memory.mjs:437), but a single `move` does not. A probe recorded `move --to rejected --by agent:claude` and `--to snoozed --by skill:dowser` on verified cards. A rejected card is in `suppressed` for its lens from then on (memory.mjs:174-176), so an agent that "tidies" a card buries it for every later scan, and trust.mjs:49 does not count it, so nobody sees the prediction it overrode.

## Flow
- agent, mid-triage, runs `move <fp> --to rejected --by agent:claude-code --reason not-worth-it`
- move checks canMove and deciderAllowed: verified>rejected is unguarded
- card becomes rejected, decided_by agent:claude-code
- every later context lists it in suppressed; outbox never pushes it; the person never saw it

## Expected impact
The "a person decides every proposal" promise holds in code, not only in the procedure. Risk: low; a forge: verdict and human: moves keep working; a test that moves with agent: or skill: for these targets must change.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the store refuses decisions the procedure reserves for people
Before: probe: 2 of 2 non-human decisions recorded (rejected by agent:claude, snoozed by skill:dowser)
After: simulation: both refused with exit 2 "needs a human decider"; human:runner reject, forge:<user> verdict, and skill:dowser wake (snoozed -> verified) still pass
Method: probe - scratch script outside the repo against a temp store with the lib move()
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:102: 'verified>accepted': Object.freeze(['human']), | skill/SKILL.md:544: - **Never self-approve.** Only a human accepts, rejects, snoozes or merges into another person's | skill/references/triage.md:14: | `verified` | `rejected` | human | `move --to rejected --reason <code>` (pre-triage) | | probe output: "rejected agent:claude -> rejected agent:claude", "snoozed skill:dowser -> snoozed skill:dowser"
impact_why: An agent decision silently suppresses a verified card forever and bypasses the trust ledger, against the stated invariant

title: Stamp provenance.lens_version from the pack at propose, as run_id is
body:
## Summary
Have `propose` set `provenance.lens_version` from the loaded pack (replacing a different one with a note, as it does for run_id), so the quality ledger and predicted_by are keyed by the pack that actually ran.

## Description
skill/references/cards.md:30 tells the agent to copy the pack `version` into provenance; skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:184-186 stamps `run_id` from `--run` and overwrites a different one, but passes `lens_version` through as written. The store then keys `quality` per lens version on it (skill/scripts/lib/quality.mjs:35) and builds `predicted_by` from it (skill/scripts/lib/predict.mjs:148). The agent has two sources for the number: the pack frontmatter and the 13 worked examples, which hard-code it (e.g. skill/references/examples/doc-drift.md:32). A pack bump that misses one example, or an agent that copies the example literally, files cards under the old version and the ledger compares the wrong versions.

## Flow
- pack bumps to 0.3.3; one example still says 0.3.2
- agent copies the example provenance
- propose stores lens_version 0.3.2 with no note
- `quality` credits 0.3.3 work to 0.3.2

## Expected impact
Per-version accept rates and prediction agreement describe the pack that ran. Risk: low; a card naming another version gets a note, not a refusal.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - lens_version on every stored card equals the pack that was loaded for propose
Before: code read: 0 checks of lens_version in proposals.mjs (grep returns nothing); run_id is stamped at :184-186
After: simulation: three cases - matching version stored as is; stale version replaced plus note; missing version filled from the pack (no more provenance.lens_version:required refusal at model.mjs:475)
Method: simulation - walked the three cases through propose; no build allowed
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:186: const provenance = clean({ ...c.provenance, run_id: runId, model: c.provenance.model ?? run.model, harness: c.provenance.harness ?? run.harness, focus: c.provenance.focus ?? run.focus }); | grep -n lens_version skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs -> (none) | skill/scripts/lib/quality.mjs:35: const version = typeof prov.lens_version === 'string' ? prov.lens_version : 'unknown'; | skill/scripts/lib/predict.mjs:148: const by = ... `dowser-${c.lens}@${c.provenance.lens_version}:${m}`
impact_why: The proposal-quality ledger is keyed by a number the agent types; one stale copy mislabels a whole run

title: A bug in dowser.mjs is reported as "store unavailable", its stack dropped
body:
## Summary
Give non-DowserError exceptions their own error code (`internal`) and print the stack on stderr, so a programming error is not read by the agent as a connection or store outage.

## Description
skill/scripts/dowser.mjs:620-621 maps every exception that is not a DowserError to exit 3 with `{error: 'unavailable', message}` and only `e.message` on stderr. SKILL.md:38 tells the agent that 3 means "store or connection unavailable ... stop that step; report it in plain words", and headless runs then `run finish --status failed` (SKILL.md:495-497). So a TypeError in a handler (a malformed saved tool response, a null field) is reported to the runner as "memory unavailable", and the stack that would locate it is gone. There is no log file, so the only trace is that message.

## Flow
- ingest-verdicts reads a response shape it does not expect
- a TypeError "Cannot read properties of undefined" escapes the handler
- main returns code 3, error unavailable, message only
- agent tells the runner the store is unavailable and stops the step

## Expected impact
Bugs surface as bugs with a location; outages keep code 3. Risk: low; the exit code can stay 3 if the procedure needs it, only `error` and stderr change.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - an internal error is distinguishable from an outage in the CLI output
Before: simulation: TypeError, SQLITE_BUSY and EACCES all print error unavailable, message only
After: simulation: SQLITE_BUSY and EACCES unchanged; TypeError prints error internal with stack on stderr
Method: simulation - walked three exception types through main(); a probe needs a broken handler
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/scripts/dowser.mjs:620: const msg = /** @type {Error} */ (e)?.message ?? String(e); | :621: return { code: 3, stdout: `${JSON.stringify({ error: 'unavailable', message: msg }, null, 2)}\n`, stderr: `dowser: ${msg}\n` }; | skill/SKILL.md:38: | 3 | store or connection unavailable, or the command is not built yet | stop that step; report it in plain words; never write the store any other way |
impact_why: Every internal bug is misreported as an outage and loses its stack, slowing diagnosis of field failures

title: No CI runs the gates; Dependabot opens PRs nothing tests
body:
## Summary
Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` (and the forge gates when forge/ changes) on push and pull request, on Node 22.13 and current.

## Description
AGENTS.md:30-38 lists the gates as something to run "before you hand back work", by hand. `git ls-files .github` returns only .github/dependabot.yml, which opens weekly npm PRs for three directories (/, /forge, /forge/static/app). No workflow, no hook (core.hooksPath unset, no non-sample hook). So every Dependabot PR, including typescript ~7.0.2 and @types/node bumps that change typecheck results, merges untested unless someone checks it out. The product plan itself names GitHub Actions as a scan runner (docs/project-documentation.md:84).

## Flow
- Dependabot opens a minor-and-patch group PR for /forge
- nothing runs; the PR shows no checks
- it is merged from the web UI
- the break shows up in the next local scan or forge deploy

## Expected impact
Dependency PRs and contributor pushes carry a red/green check; the Node 22.13 floor (node:sqlite) is tested, not assumed. Risk: low; adds a workflow file only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every PR runs the gates AGENTS.md names
Before: 0 workflows; 3 Dependabot ecosystems weekly, up to 15 open PRs, 0 checks
After: each PR shows typecheck and test status (simulation over a dependabot PR, a doc-only push and a forge change)
Method: gate - listed .github and hooks; the workflow run itself needs GitHub
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: git ls-files .github -> .github/dependabot.yml (only) | .github/dependabot.yml: package-ecosystem: npm, directory: "/", "/forge", "/forge/static/app", interval: weekly, open-pull-requests-limit: 5 | AGENTS.md:32: Run both before you hand back work: | git config --get core.hooksPath -> (unset)
impact_why: Up to 15 automated dependency PRs at a time merge with no test signal; the gates exist but nothing runs them

title: Cut a release: 55 commits since v0.2.0, so --check calls old installs current
body:
## Summary
Bump SKILL.md and package.json past 0.2.0 and tag a release, so `install.mjs --check` tells a v0.2.0 install that hydrate, build mode, delivery and the work queue exist.

## Description
skill/SKILL.md:7 and package.json:3 both say 0.2.0, the tag v0.2.0 is from 2026-10-30, and `git log v0.2.0..HEAD` counts 55 commits, 19 of them in skill/SKILL.md or skill/scripts/lib (memory pull and hydrate, delivery, build mode, edges, quality ledger). `--check` compares the installed version with the newest tag (skill/install.mjs:211 `behind = Boolean(lv && (!cur || cmp(cur, lv) < 0))`), so a copy installed at v0.2.0 is reported up to date. The Forge app meanwhile is deployed with tools that only the new SKILL.md calls (dowser_memory_pull, dowser_work_*).

## Flow
- teammate installed the skill from v0.2.0
- runs `npm run check-update`
- behind: false
- their first run on a new machine skips hydrate (no section 3 step 0 in their copy) and re-proposes what the team rejected

## Expected impact
Installed copies learn when they are behind the procedure the Forge app expects. Risk: low; a version bump and a tag.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - --check reports a v0.2.0 copy as behind
Before: simulation: installed 0.2.0 vs newest tag v0.2.0 -> behind false
After: simulation: installed 0.2.0 vs v0.3.0 -> behind true with the update notice
Method: simulation - walked install.mjs:211 with both tag sets; tagging is the build
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/SKILL.md:7: version: 0.2.0 | package.json:3: "version": "0.2.0", | git log --oneline v0.2.0..HEAD | wc -l -> 55; -- skill/SKILL.md skill/scripts/lib -> 19; git log -1 --format=%ad v0.2.0 -> 2026-10-30 | skill/install.mjs:211: const behind = Boolean(lv && (!cur || cmp(cur, lv) < 0));
impact_why: The update check is blind to two weeks of procedure changes the Forge app already relies on
